tls_echo_server Example

TLS server using gxsTLSServer and a ThreadPool. Usage: tls_echo_server port cert.pem key.pem

Contents

Building and Running
Source

Building and Running

examples/tls/tls_echo_server.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as tls_echo_server (cmake-build/examples/tls_echo_server on Linux, cmake-build\examples\Release\tls_echo_server.exe on Windows) and run by tests/run_tests.sh. See Building and Running for the build commands. The comment at the top of the file describes the program. Back to the example programs.

TLS echo server. Each client runs on a datareel::ThreadPool worker
and every line it sends is sent back. A client that sends "quit"
is disconnected, and "shutdown" stops the server.

Usage: tls_echo_server port cert.pem key.pem [threads]
*/
// ----------------------------------------------------------- // 
#include "gxdlcode.h"

#include <atomic>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <iostream>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include "gxstls.h"
#include "thrpool.h"

using namespace datareel;

static std::mutex console_mutex;
static std::atomic<bool> stopping(false);

static void say(const std::string &s)
{
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(console_mutex);
  std::cout << s << std::endl;
}

static void serve_client(std::shared_ptr<gxsTLSConnection> conn, int port)
{
  std::string peer = conn->Socket().PeerAddress().ToString();
  say("Client connected: " + peer);
  std::string line;
  while(conn->ReadLine(line)) {
    if(line == "quit") break;
    if(line == "shutdown") {
      stopping = true;
      conn->SendLine("Server shutting down");
      // Wake the accept() call with a connection of our own
      gxSocket wake;
      wake.Connect("localhost", port, 5);
      break;
    }
    if(conn->SendLine(line) < 0) break;
  }
  conn->Close();
  say("Client disconnected: " + peer);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
  if(argc < 4) {
    std::cerr << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " port cert.pem key.pem [threads]\n";
    return 1;
  }
  int port = std::atoi(argv[1]);
  std::size_t threads = argc > 4 ? (std::size_t)std::atoi(argv[4]) : 4;

  gxsTLSServer server;
  if(server.Listen(port, argv[2], argv[3]) != 0) {
    std::cerr << server.Error() << "\n";
    return 1;
  }
  say("Listening on port " + std::to_string(server.Port()));

  ThreadPool pool(threads);
  while(!stopping) {
    auto conn = std::make_shared<gxsTLSConnection>();
    conn->SetTimeout(300);
    if(server.Accept(*conn) != 0) {
      if(!stopping) say("Accept failed: " + server.Error());
      continue;
    }
    if(stopping) break;
    pool.Submit(serve_client, conn, port);
  }
  pool.Wait();
  server.Close();
  say("Server stopped");
  return 0;
}
